Can't Find the Model You Want in Claude Code's /model Menu? Try This Trick
Can't find a model with Claude Code /model? Switch by entering the full model ID
A new model just came out, but maybe you don't actually want to use it. Or maybe the model you do want isn't showing up when you run
. Here's a small trick that lets you use the model you want in Claude Code anyway.
If you've used Claude Code, you probably already know that the
The list will usually give you options like these:
. But if you want to use a different model, you may run into a problem: the model you want simply isn't listed under
command only lists the models Claude Code officially recommends. Other available models won't appear in the menu.

Why does this happen? Basically, model providers want you on the version they recommend, since that's usually the most stable and best-supported option. So the other models stay hidden from the default list.
That can still be a problem, though. The most common reason is pretty simple:
The new model isn't as good as you expected.
Take Opus 4.8 as an example. Plenty of people felt that Opus 4.8 wasn't as good as Opus 4.6 or 4.7, so they preferred to keep using one of those older versions.
The trick: pass the model ID to /model
command — we're just skipping the menu.
Say you want to use Opus 4.8. Open Claude Code and enter the following directly in the conversation:
language-bash shiki shiki-themes github-light github-light github-dark-high-contrast
Claude Code switching to the selected model
The model ID has to be exact. You can find the available IDs in Anthropic's official
That page also tells you when each model will stop being supported. If the model you want has already reached end of support, you'll need to pick another one.
If you don't want a future Claude Code update to quietly change your model again, you can pin it in
language-json shiki shiki-themes github-light github-light github-dark-high-contrast
precedence in mind: system settings take priority over user settings.
And that's it — a small trick for keeping Claude Code on the model you actually want.
